final_candidates.decision_summary: Charge reversal at a predicted m102.4-class contact residue likely disrupts antibody salt-bridge interactions while leaving ephrin-B2/B3 binding largely intact.
Glycine substitution removes an acidic side chain and increases loop flexibility in the receptor-binding-site proximal region, impairing antibody recognition without abolishing receptor engagement.
Asn retains steric bulk but removes the negative charge at D512, providing an alternative m102.4 escape mutation that may better preserve ephrin binding.

stop_reason.detail: The current Top-3 candidates are strongly supported by structural reasoning and additional self-iteration is unlikely to improve their ranking.

history.rationale: Surface-exposed C-terminal RBD rim residue likely to contact m102.4-class antibodies but not the core ephrin-B2/B3 binding residues E463/Y511/I518.
Retained as a C-terminal tail candidate but ranked below receptor-binding-site proximal substitutions.
Extreme C-terminal residue near the RBD; alanine substitution may disrupt antibody contacts while preserving receptor binding.
C-terminal residue may affect antibody binding but is less likely to be a primary escape determinant.
Charged residue adjacent to the receptor-binding pocket that may form antibody-specific contacts; alanine removal likely spares core receptor residues.
Kept as secondary candidate; charged residue near C-terminal tail may influence antibody contacts.
Basic surface residue on the C-terminal RBD rim predicted to modulate m102.4-class binding without eliminating ephrin binding.
Moderate confidence; charged C-terminal residue may contribute to epitope but not as strongly as D512/E509.
Acidic residue near the C-terminus of the RBD; charge removal may weaken antibody contacts while leaving ephrin-B2/B3 interface intact.
C-terminal acidic residue retained with lower priority due to uncertain antibody relevance.
Hydrophobic residue near the RBD rim; alanine substitution could reduce antibody heavy-chain packing contacts without affecting core ephrin binding.
Hydrophobic C-terminal residue kept but lower confidence for selective escape.
Hydrophobic C-terminal residue adjacent to the RBD; predicted antibody-contact position with lower probability of receptor-binding impairment.
Lower-priority C-terminal candidate; less likely to specifically affect m102.4-class binding.
Acidic residue in a loop near the critical Y511/I518 region; may contribute more to antibody binding than to ephrin receptor binding.
Removed to make room for stronger receptor-binding-site proximal candidates; D515 is less supported for m102.4 escape.

rejection.reason: Removed to make room for stronger receptor-binding-site proximal candidates; D515 is less supported for m102.4 escape.

history.rationale: Loop residue near the receptor-binding pocket; potential m102.4 contact whose substitution may preserve sufficient ephrin binding.
Lower confidence and less likely to provide selective escape while preserving receptor binding.

rejection.reason: Lower confidence and less likely to provide selective escape while preserving receptor binding.

history.rationale: Adjacent to the critical E463 residue but not a core receptor-binding residue; may alter local antibody contact while retaining receptor function.
Too distant from the likely m102.4/receptor-binding interface and lower confidence for the target phenotype.
